title: People’s Mañanera August 13
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Mexico is in Vogue Trending and Breaking Tourism Records  
** Between January and June, a record 51.1 million international travelers
arrived in Mexico. The World Cup boosted tourism by more than 33% in the host
cities, and 40% of visitors were motivated by the country's cultural
attractions.

**The Morning Presidential Press Conference Belongs to the People  
** In response to the PAN's request for the right of reply during the Morning
Presidential Press Conference, Sheinbaum explained that "this is a space for
the people, where the Government of Mexico fulfills its responsibility to
inform the public." "Let them hold their own press conference; there they can
have a proper right of reply," she added.

**Freedom of Expression to the Fullest  
** The President reiterated that she will not censor anyone and defended
"freedom of expression, but also the right of reply." Sheinbaum highlighted
that 79% believe that fake news should be penalized and reminded everyone that
"only a fool believes the people are fools."

**Sheinbaum Questions Alito for Traveling to the U.S.  
** Sheinbaum criticized Alito Moreno, leader of "a political party on the
verge of extinction," for traveling to the United States to request that
Mexican officials' visas be revoked. "It's downright laughable." She added
that the PRI senator doesn't have much credibility here and probably not there
either.

**It 's Not Political Persecution, Sheinbaum Says  
**Regarding the arrests of officials linked to Alito, the President commented
that "this is a question of crime, of offenses that were committed." She
clarified that the investigation falls under the jurisdiction of the Campeche
State Attorney General's Office, not the Federal Attorney General's Office
(FGR), and that any removal of immunity is the responsibility of Congress.
